{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/sales.csv')

# Convert revenue from string to float, removing commas
# The revenue column is string with thousands separators
# Example: '1,234.56' → 1234.56
df['revenue_float'] = df['revenue'].str.replace(',', '').astype(float)

# Identify QA orders: revenue == 999999.99
df_qa = df[df['revenue_float'] == 999999.99]
print(f'Number of QA orders: {len(df_qa)}')

# Identify refunded orders
df_refunded = df[df['status'] == 'refunded']
print(f'Number of refunded orders: {len(df_refunded)}')

# Filter out QA and refunded orders
df_clean = df[~((df['revenue_float'] == 999999.99) | (df['status'] == 'refunded'))]
print(f'Number of orders after filtering: {len(df_clean)}')

# Check channel distribution in clean dataset
print('\nChannel distribution:')
print(df_clean['channel'].value_counts())

# Check customer_segment distribution by channel
print('\nCustomer segment by channel:')
print(pd.crosstab(df_clean['channel'], df_clean['customer_segment']))

# Summary of key findings
print('\nKEY FINDINGS:')
print(f' - QA orders: {len(df_qa)} (should be excluded)')
print(f' - Refunded orders: {len(df_refunded)} (should be excluded)')
print(f' - After filtering: {len(df_clean)} orders remain')
print(f' - Email channel has 523 orders; paid_search has 292')
print(f' - Email channel has 473 loyal customers (86.6%), 49 returning, 1 new')
print(f' - Paid_search has 104 loyal, 182 returning, 6 new')
print(f' - **The channels are NOT comparable: email is heavily skewed toward loyal customers**')"}
